_doc: FABLE-068: the class starting zones' encounters. Generated by tools/gen_start_zones.py.

encounters.name: Sealwright Tamsin Vey
dialogue_intro: Sealwick, on the Unmade Coast at the edge of the Void. Beyond the last fence the rain falls upward and the river stands on its side.
A woman in a patched raiding coat chalks a seal on the gatepost without looking up. "New blood. Good. Hit me — the Void won't wait for you to be ready."
dialogue_outro: Tamsin rubs out the chalk and nods. "You'll do for the Coast. Don't go in alone yet."

encounters.name: The Breach Golem
dialogue_intro: Where the Void last pushed through, the ground healed wrong. Something stone and seal-script has stood up out of the scar.
It was raised by the old raiders to hold the Breach. It still thinks you are the Void.
dialogue_outro: The golem kneels and goes still, its seal-runes dimming to grey. The Breach is quiet behind it.
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: Marrow the Breach-Broker
dialogue_intro: Not everything that comes out of the Void is a monster. Some of it is for sale.
A man with a Void-glass eye spreads his wares on a cloth: bottled rain, a knife that is in two places. "Sealwick pays me not to sell these. You haven't."
dialogue_outro: Marrow packs his cloth, careful of the knife. "Fine. Fine. Keep your Coast. I'll find another edge."
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: Brine-Warder Ilsa Crane
dialogue_intro: The Upstairs River runs beside the road, its surface a wall of standing water. A warder paces it with a ward-staff.
"The river wards itself; I only help. Strike all you like — it gives back what it takes."
dialogue_outro: Her ward bursts like a wave on rock. "Well," Ilsa says, dripping. "The river was wrong."
lesson: WARD
WARD blocks the next damage, once. Pop it with a small hit or a cheap spell before you send in something big.

encounters.name: Tidecaller Pell of the Stitchline
dialogue_intro: A seal-tower on the Stitchline, its bell cracked. The caller inside has been reading the Void's tides too long.
"It's beautiful in there, you know. It only wants to come through. Who are we to stitch it shut?"
dialogue_outro: Pell's chant breaks and the tide behind the tower slides back off the Unmade Coast. He sits down, very tired.
lesson: RITUALS
A card with no Strength and no Vigor is a Ritual: it resolves the moment it is played. This foe leans on them — spread your board so one spell can't undo it.

encounters.name: Captain Orran, Who Came Back
dialogue_intro: Three seasons ago Captain Orran led a band into the Void. Yesterday he walked out of it alone.
He is taller than he was. His shadow points the wrong way. "Sealwick owes me a band," he says. "You'll do as a start."
dialogue_outro: Orran drops to one knee, and for a moment his shadow lies the right way. "Seal it behind me," he says. "Please."
lesson: PIERCE
PIERCE: damage past a killed blocker carries on to the player. Chump-blocking with a tiny creature will not fully save you.

encounters.name: Archivist Corran Vey
dialogue_intro: Under Sealwick lies the seal-archive: every stitch ever made, in Tamsin's family's hand.
"Every spell you cast, I have already catalogued. Show me something the Void hasn't."
dialogue_outro: Corran scribbles furiously. "A new entry. How thrilling. How humiliating."
lesson: READ THE TABLE
Along the top you can see how many cards your foe is holding. A full hand late in a fight usually means something big is coming — keep a blocker back.

encounters.name: Warden Seraphine of the Quiet Gate
dialogue_intro: The Quiet Gate is the first seal — the one every other stitch is anchored to. One woman keeps it.
"Raiders come every season. Few pass me. Show me you can hold a spell with the Void looking at you."
dialogue_outro: Seraphine steps back from the gate. "Then come through. See what I have been holding back."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Seraphine, the First Stitch
dialogue_intro: The Gate opens. Beyond it the Void waits, and Seraphine stands in it as if in her own kitchen.
"Sealwick was a city once, not a village. I stitched it shut around the Breach — and I would do it again."
dialogue_outro: The Void settles like water. Seraphine kneels on the shore. "The road is open past the Gate. Beyond it, the Cinderfall Steps. Go — and come home for dinner."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: Rain-Caller Wenna
dialogue_intro: On Gull Stair the rain falls upward into a cloud that never moves. A woman stands under it, catching nothing.
"Every drop that goes up is one the Void keeps. Help me bring them down - the hard way."
dialogue_outro: Wenna lowers her hands, and for the first time in a year the rain on Gull Stair falls down.

encounters.name: Salvager Druce
dialogue_intro: A wreck-picker has claimed Mist Horn, and everything the Void washes onto it.
"Finders keepers. You found me, so I suppose that makes you mine."
dialogue_outro: Druce tosses you a sea-glass coin. "Fair's fair. The beach is yours till the next tide."

encounters.name: The Seal-Eater
dialogue_intro: Something on Low Fang has been gnawing the old raiders' seals off the stones, one by one.
It turns. It has a mouth where its face should be, and the chalk-dust of a hundred seals on its teeth.
dialogue_outro: The thing comes apart into chalk and rain. Behind it, the gnawed seals on Low Fang begin to glow again.

encounters.name: Lamp-Keeper Abel
dialogue_intro: The light on Sounding Vault has burned the wrong colour since the last Breach. Its keeper lets no one near it.
"It shows the Void the way in. I know. But it's MY light."
dialogue_outro: Abel lets the lamp go dark and sits down on the stair. "Light it again in the morning," he says. "The right colour."

encounters.name: Bone-Keeper Hobb
dialogue_intro: The Undercroft of Greyvault: level under level of the dead, and the bells of the cathedral overhead, always ringing.
An old keeper leans on his spade at the top of the Bone Stair. "New to the under, are you? Let's see if you can wake more than dust."
dialogue_outro: Hobb nods slowly. "You'll do. The dead are watching you now. Be polite."

encounters.name: The Ossuary Sentinel
dialogue_intro: A sentinel of stacked skulls blocks the stair to the second level.
It was built to stand, not to think — and it stands very well.
dialogue_outro: The sentinel topples, skulls rolling down the stair like dice. Somewhere above, a bell misses a beat.
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: Purger Halvard of the Ward
dialogue_intro: A knight of the cathedral upstairs has come down the Sealed Door's forgotten side-stair, lantern first.
"Every corpse you raise is a soul you steal. I will put them back to rest — and you with them."
dialogue_outro: Halvard's lantern gutters. "The Lantern-Mother will hear of this," he gasps, and goes back up the way he came.
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: The Twice-Buried
dialogue_intro: The floor heaves. Something that was buried twice has decided not to stay that way.
Bury it once and it climbs back. You will have to bury it again.
dialogue_outro: This time it stays down. Mostly.
lesson: UNEARTH
Some creatures claw their way back out of the Barrow — that is UNEARTH. Killing one may not be the end of it.

encounters.name: Widow Rotbloom of the Quiet Choir
dialogue_intro: In the Quiet Choir, where the dead hum, nightshade grows from the graves of poisoners.
The widow tending them smiles. "Every bloom here killed someone. Care to smell one?"
dialogue_outro: The widow wilts among her flowers. The Choir hums one note lower.
lesson: VENOM
VENOM: anything it damages in combat is destroyed. Don't trade your best creature into it — block with something small, or kill it with a ritual.

encounters.name: Lantern-Mother Mirel
dialogue_intro: The Purger's mistress comes down herself, a procession of lanterns behind her, through a door that was sealed.
"Greyvault was holy ground before your kind crept under it. It will be again."
dialogue_outro: The lanterns gutter one by one. Mirel lowers her staff. "Not today, then. But the dawn always comes — even down here."
lesson: SWIFT
SWIFT creatures can attack the turn they arrive. Keep a blocker up — and use your own to finish a foe that thinks it is safe.

encounters.name: Bone-Scribe Ettrin
dialogue_intro: A rival keeper records every death in Greyvault in a ledger bound in skin.
"Your name is not in my book yet. Let's correct that."
dialogue_outro: Ettrin tears a page out of his ledger — the one with your name half-written.
lesson: READ THE TABLE
Along the top you can see how many cards your foe is holding. A full hand late in a fight usually means something big is coming — keep a blocker back.

encounters.name: Warden Corvane, Keeper of the Lowest Stair
dialogue_intro: At the bottom of the Bone Stair the Keeper decides who may command the dead.
"Many can wake a corpse. Few can make it obey. Show me."
dialogue_outro: Corvane's thralls kneel — to you. "Interesting," he says. "Come down to the last door."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Corvane, the Pale Sovereign
dialogue_intro: The Keeper sheds his robe. Beneath is bone, and an old light burning in empty sockets.
"I have kept the Undercroft for three hundred years. I did not do it by losing."
dialogue_outro: The light in Corvane's eyes dims. "The under is yours. Beyond the last door, the Cinderfall Steps — go and be feared there."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: Grave-Robber Mott
dialogue_intro: Fresh earth on Crow Pass, and a shovel still standing in it.
"Nobody down here's using it," says the man with the sack. "Bones are bones."
dialogue_outro: Mott drops the sack. It rattles. "Put 'em back yourself, then."

encounters.name: The Unquiet Ferrywoman
dialogue_intro: On Sorrow Peak a woman in a sodden shroud waits beside a boat with no bottom.
"The fare is a memory. Yours will do."
dialogue_outro: She pushes off into the mist without you. "Another time," drifts back across the water.

encounters.name: Brother Candle
dialogue_intro: A monk of the Ward keeps vigil on Dusk Crag, a candle in each hand and a hammer in his belt.
"Nothing dead walks past my light. Are you dead? Let's find out."
dialogue_outro: Brother Candle's flames gutter. "Alive," he says, surprised. "Mostly. Go on."

encounters.name: The Ossified Hound
dialogue_intro: Something on Hollow Fang is digging. Bone scrapes on bone.
A hound made of a dozen hounds lifts its head from the hole and growls without breath.
dialogue_outro: The hound falls into a neat pile of bones, as if it had only been waiting to be told to rest.

encounters.name: Squire-Captain Bram
dialogue_intro: The Lantern Yard of Greyvault: the dead laid in the open under a thousand lamps, and the bells that never stop.
"On guard, recruit. The light helps those who keep their shield up."
dialogue_outro: Bram lowers his practice blade. "Good. Now go and swear it at the Oath-Stone, for real."

encounters.name: Gatewarden Hesk
dialogue_intro: An old soldier holds the Ward's gate, as he has for twenty years.
"Nobody crosses my gate without showing me their shield-work."
dialogue_outro: Hesk steps aside, rubbing his shield arm. "That'll do. Mind the lanterns."
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: Sir Vael, Oath-Broken
dialogue_intro: A knight in tarnished gold has turned his sword on the Order that raised him.
"Oaths are chains, child. I broke mine. Let me show you how."
dialogue_outro: Vael's blade cracks across the Oath-Stone. He does not get up.
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: Lantern-Sister Lumen
dialogue_intro: A sister of the Vigil bars the cloister walk, wrapped in wards of lamplight.
"The light is not yours alone. Prove you deserve it."
dialogue_outro: Her wards fade like morning mist. "Go in light, then," she says, and means it.
lesson: WARD
WARD blocks the next damage, once. Pop it with a small hit or a cheap spell before you send in something big.

encounters.name: The Gilded Bulwark
dialogue_intro: A war-construct of the Old Age, armoured in plates of beaten gold, stands in the Bell Tower's shadow.
It was made to outlast sieges. It has outlasted its makers.
dialogue_outro: The Bulwark grinds to a halt, one golden fist still raised in salute.
lesson: ARMOR
ARMOR takes that much less damage from every hit. Many small hits do little — hit it once, and hit it hard.

encounters.name: Kesh of the Hungry Sands
dialogue_intro: Raiders from the far south have struck the outer chapels and emptied the reliquaries.
"Gold and bones sell the same in Tamunet. Yours will too."
dialogue_outro: Kesh drops the stolen relics and runs for the gate. The bells ring out behind you.
lesson: SWIFT
SWIFT creatures can attack the turn they arrive. Keep a blocker up — and use your own to finish a foe that thinks it is safe.

encounters.name: Inquisitor Aldric
dialogue_intro: An inquisitor of the Vigil questions every knight who would stand at the Sealed Door.
"Faith untested is only habit. Let us test yours."
dialogue_outro: Aldric bows his head. "Tested, and true. Go on."
lesson: READ THE TABLE
Along the top you can see how many cards your foe is holding. A full hand late in a fight usually means something big is coming — keep a blocker back.

encounters.name: Warden Dawnhild of the Sealed Door
dialogue_intro: Before the Sealed Door, the High Warden keeps the first lantern.
"Every knight of Greyvault stood where you stand. Not all of them walked away."
dialogue_outro: Dawnhild lowers her shield. "Then face me at the door itself."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Dawnhild, the Unbroken Wall
dialogue_intro: The first lantern flares around her like wings. Behind her, the Sealed Door hums.
"I have never yielded a step. Not to what is under this hill, and not to you."
dialogue_outro: For the first time in her life, Dawnhild yields a step. "The Ward is yours, knight. The Cinderfall Steps wait beyond. Keep the door shut behind you."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: Sister Ashlin, Penitent
dialogue_intro: A penitent kneels on Bright Heart, wearing her own armour backwards.
"I swore an oath I could not keep. Strike me until it feels kept."
dialogue_outro: Ashlin rises and turns her armour the right way round. "Thank you. It's heavier like this."

encounters.name: Toll-Knight Garrow
dialogue_intro: A knight has strung a toll-chain across Gold Scree, and nobody remembers giving him the right.
"One coin, or one fight. I'm hoping you're short of coin."
dialogue_outro: Garrow unhooks the chain. "Keep the coin. That was worth more."

encounters.name: The Hollow Reliquary
dialogue_intro: On Noon Fang a reliquary has cracked open, and what was kept inside is walking.
It wears a saint's ring on every finger, and none of them are its own.
dialogue_outro: The relic-thing kneels and stills. The rings slide off, one by one, back into the box.

encounters.name: Pilgrim Rhosyn
dialogue_intro: A pilgrim has stopped on Clear Pass and planted something where she stopped.
"The Ward wants walls. I want a garden. Let's see which grows faster."
dialogue_outro: Rhosyn laughs and takes up her staff. "A garden, then. When you're done with the walls."

encounters.name: Bough-Keeper Tamsin
dialogue_intro: The Boughs of Yrmund, the Walking Tree. Below, the Rootwake — a league of torn ground and new forest for every season the tree has walked.
"The roots told me you were coming. Show me you can listen back."
dialogue_outro: Tamsin smiles. "The tree likes you. Don't make it change its mind."

encounters.name: The Bark-Hide Bear
dialogue_intro: A bear with bark for a hide stands across the Rootwake, guarding a den Yrmund tore open last spring.
It does not want to fight. It will, though.
dialogue_outro: The bear lumbers back into its den, grumbling. The path along the wake is clear.
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: Timber-Lord Garran
dialogue_intro: Saws and chains hang from the fallen boughs. Someone wants the tree to stop walking.
"A tree that size is a fortune in planks. Druids fetch a fine price too."
dialogue_outro: You cut the chains. The beasts of the Rootwake scatter into the green, and Garran's crew with them.
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: The Wake-Pack
dialogue_intro: Eyes in the new growth. Then many eyes. The wolves that follow the tree are hungry this season.
The pack moves before you can count them.
dialogue_outro: The pack melts back into the wake. Somewhere, a wolf howls — almost respectfully.
lesson: SWIFT
SWIFT creatures can attack the turn they arrive. Keep a blocker up — and use your own to finish a foe that thinks it is safe.

encounters.name: Blightcaller Venn
dialogue_intro: Where he walks the new growth turns grey and the saplings weep black sap. Blight follows the tree; he follows the blight.
"Everything the tree tears up was buried for a reason. I'm only helping it rot."
dialogue_outro: Venn falls, and green creeps back over the grey where he stood.
lesson: VENOM
VENOM: anything it damages in combat is destroyed. Don't trade your best creature into it — block with something small, or kill it with a ritual.

encounters.name: The Rot-Hart
dialogue_intro: A great stag, its antlers hung with grave-moss, stalks the blighted stretch of the wake.
The blight has taken it. Put it to rest.
dialogue_outro: The Rot-Hart lies down among the ferns. Flowers open where it fell.
lesson: PIERCE
PIERCE: damage past a killed blocker carries on to the player. Chump-blocking with a tiny creature will not fully save you.

encounters.name: Hedge-Witch Morrow of the Fallen Bough
dialogue_intro: A limb Yrmund shed long ago has grown into a village of its own. Its witch trades in favours from the wild.
"You want through my hedge? Pay in sweat."
dialogue_outro: Morrow's hedge parts with a sigh. "Paid in full. Off you go."
lesson: READ THE TABLE
Along the top you can see how many cards your foe is holding. A full hand late in a fight usually means something big is coming — keep a blocker back.

encounters.name: Warden Oakheart of the Heartwood Stair
dialogue_intro: The oldest Druid in the Boughs opens his eyes at the top of the Heartwood Stair.
"I have watched saplings grow for a hundred years. Grow, little sapling. Show me."
dialogue_outro: Oakheart creaks with something like laughter. "Then come down to the roots."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Oakheart, Voice of the Source
dialogue_intro: The ground splits. Oakheart stands at the Source-Well, and the tree's roots move when he does.
"Yrmund is walking toward something. You will not turn it. Neither will I."
dialogue_outro: Oakheart settles, a forest at peace. "The tree will remember you. Walk ahead of it — the Cinderfall Steps are next."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: The Moss-Back Elk
dialogue_intro: On Elder Stair an elk older than the trees has grown moss to its knees.
It lowers antlers hung with nests and lets you know whose ground this is.
dialogue_outro: The elk snorts, satisfied, and wades back into the green of Elder Stair.

encounters.name: Fungal Shepherd Ivo
dialogue_intro: Pale caps grow in rings on Deep Fang, and a man in a mushroom-cloth cloak tends them.
"They only eat the dead parts of the wood. You look a little dead around the edges."
dialogue_outro: Ivo's rings wilt. "Fine. The wood keeps its dead. For now."

encounters.name: Woodcutter Hask
dialogue_intro: Stumps all across Green Crag, fresh-cut, and an axe still singing in the last one.
"Trees grow back," says the woodcutter. "So will you, maybe."
dialogue_outro: Hask shoulders his axe and looks at the stumps as if for the first time. "I'll plant some," he mutters.

encounters.name: The Thornwife
dialogue_intro: A woman made of bramble sits on Moss Vault, singing to the thorns.
"The wake took my orchard. I'll take something back."
dialogue_outro: The Thornwife's song softens to a hum, and a single white flower opens on Moss Vault.

encounters.name: Fence-Mother Agathe
dialogue_intro: Tamunet, in the Hungry Sands: tomb-temples older than kingdoms, a living town crammed into their shadows, and no river.
"So you want to run with the Gullet crews. Lift my purse, little rat — if you can."
dialogue_outro: Agathe checks her belt and finds it lighter. "Ha! Welcome to the family. Eat something."

encounters.name: Tomb-Guard Bolsover
dialogue_intro: A hulking guard minds the door of the first tomb-temple, paid by the night and paid well.
"Nobody gets past old Bolsover. Nobody."
dialogue_outro: Bolsover wakes up an hour later with his keys missing and no idea why.
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: The Lamp-Snuffer
dialogue_intro: Every lamp in the Salt Market goes out at once. Someone is very good at this.
"You're in my dark now."
dialogue_outro: You strike a light. The Snuffer is gone — but so is the dark.
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: Quickfinger Lisle
dialogue_intro: A pickpocket half your age darts out of the crowd on Tomb Row.
"Race you to the bottom of your pockets!"
dialogue_outro: Lisle hands back your coin purse with a wink. "Fair's fair. You're faster."
lesson: SWIFT
SWIFT creatures can attack the turn they arrive. Keep a blocker up — and use your own to finish a foe that thinks it is safe.

encounters.name: Nightshade Priest Ozias
dialogue_intro: The priest of the Dry River temple brews poison in the offering cup.
"A sip for the faithful. A gulp for thieves."
dialogue_outro: Ozias chokes on his own sermon. You leave the cup well alone.
lesson: VENOM
VENOM: anything it damages in combat is destroyed. Don't trade your best creature into it — block with something small, or kill it with a ritual.

encounters.name: Sexton Graul's Diggers
dialogue_intro: A rival crew has claimed the lower tombs, and they don't share.
"These dead are spoken for, rat."
dialogue_outro: The diggers scatter into the tunnels, leaving their loot — and their shovels.
lesson: PIERCE
PIERCE: damage past a killed blocker carries on to the player. Chump-blocking with a tiny creature will not fully save you.

encounters.name: Veilwalker Sable
dialogue_intro: A thief who is there, then not, then behind you.
"You'll never land a hit on what you can't see."
dialogue_outro: Sable is suddenly very easy to see, sitting in the sand. "...Lucky."
lesson: DODGE
DODGE gives a chance to take no combat damage at all. Rituals are the surer answer.

encounters.name: Warden Mortimer, Master of Keys
dialogue_intro: The Guild's Master of Keys guards the stair down the Needle, the tallest tomb of all.
"Every lock in Tamunet answers to me. Let's see if you do."
dialogue_outro: Mortimer tosses you a key. "The Needle, then. He's waiting at the bottom."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Mortimer, Guildmaster of Knives
dialogue_intro: At the bottom of the Needle the vault door swings open on a man with a knife for every finger.
"I taught half this city to steal. I'll teach you to lose."
dialogue_outro: Mortimer bows from the floor. "The Gullet is yours, Guildmaster. Go rob the Cinderfall Steps for me."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: Dune-Strider Oyelaran
dialogue_intro: Footprints cross Crow Clearing and stop. The man who made them is standing behind you.
"The Sands eat the slow. Let's see how slow you are."
dialogue_outro: Oyelaran grins and is gone, leaving footprints that start nowhere.

encounters.name: The Sand-Sworn Thief
dialogue_intro: On Rust Mouth a thief is burying something that keeps trying to climb out.
"Don't look at it. Look at me. Look at my knives."
dialogue_outro: The thief bolts. Whatever was buried stays buried, which is probably for the best.

encounters.name: Tomb-Cat Mehet
dialogue_intro: A wrapped and gilded cat the size of a horse is sunning itself on Hollow Foothills.
It opens one gold eye. Then the other. It stretches. That is never good.
dialogue_outro: Mehet yawns, decides you are not worth the trouble, and curls back up on Hollow Foothills.

encounters.name: Cartographer Pell
dialogue_intro: A mapmaker sits on Sorrow Crag, drawing roads that aren't there yet.
"Anything I draw, the Sands believe. I'm drawing a road that goes through you."
dialogue_outro: Pell scrubs out the line. "Around you, then. Hold still while I redraw."

encounters.name: Current-Reader Ulla
dialogue_intro: Penumbra Camp, on the far side of the Moon. Ulmaren hangs below the horizon; the deep sky fills the rest.
"The currents said you'd land tonight. Let's see if they also said you'd win."
dialogue_outro: Ulla marks a new point on her chart. "You're on the map now."

encounters.name: The Orrery Sentinel
dialogue_intro: A great brass orrery, Old Age work, has woken and set itself to guard the Current-Stair.
Its planets wheel faster as you approach.
dialogue_outro: The planets slow, then stop. The sentinel ticks once, and is still.
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: Eclipse-Cultist Morwen
dialogue_intro: Robed figures chant on the Eclipse Field, calling for the sun to go out on Ulmaren.
"When the eclipse comes, every star you lean on goes dark."
dialogue_outro: The chanting stops. Below the horizon, the world's sun comes back one ray at a time.
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: The Star-Fallen Hermit
dialogue_intro: An old hermit lives in a crater where something fell from the deep sky. The light never quite left him.
"It spoke to me as it fell. It said you'd be trouble."
dialogue_outro: The hermit chuckles. "It was right, you know. It's always right."
lesson: WARD
WARD blocks the next damage, once. Pop it with a small hit or a cheap spell before you send in something big.

encounters.name: Lunar Acolyte Sera
dialogue_intro: An acolyte from the Unmade Coast practises her sealing rites on the Lens's terrace, far from home.
"The Moon pulls the tide. Let's see what it pulls out of you."
dialogue_outro: Sera's rite falls apart in silver dust. "Next sailing," she promises.
lesson: RITUALS
A card with no Strength and no Vigor is a Ritual: it resolves the moment it is played. This foe leans on them — spread your board so one spell can't undo it.

encounters.name: The Starborn Colossus
dialogue_intro: Something made of night and constellations climbs over the crater rim.
It fell from the deep sky long ago. It wants to go home.
dialogue_outro: The colossus breaks apart into stars, and they rise on the current — home at last.
lesson: SWIFT
SWIFT creatures can attack the turn they arrive. Keep a blocker up — and use your own to finish a foe that thinks it is safe.

encounters.name: Void-Gazer Teodric
dialogue_intro: A scholar has stared into the dark between the stars for far too long.
"There is nothing there, you know. Nothing at all. It's beautiful."
dialogue_outro: Teodric blinks, as if waking. "Oh. You're still here. How... bright."
lesson: READ THE TABLE
Along the top you can see how many cards your foe is holding. A full hand late in a fight usually means something big is coming — keep a blocker back.

encounters.name: Warden Celestine of the Lens
dialogue_intro: At the Lens, the great observatory, the Warden decides who may sail the currents.
"I chart every fate that passes through Penumbra. Yours ends here — or begins."
dialogue_outro: Celestine looks up from the Lens. "Begins, then. Come up to the dome."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Celestine, Who Turns the Heavens
dialogue_intro: The dome opens on the Unlit Crater. The stars wheel overhead at her command.
"The heavens obey me. Shall I bring them down on you?"
dialogue_outro: The sky settles back into its old shape. "The Farside is yours. Sail for Ulmaren — the Cinderfall Steps are waiting, and they burn."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: Comet-Watcher Ines
dialogue_intro: On Salt Tree a woman lies on her back, counting stars that fall the wrong way.
"One of them landed here. I'd like it back. You're standing on it."
dialogue_outro: Ines pockets a warm, glowing stone. "Thank you. It wanted to go home."

encounters.name: The Tide-Clock
dialogue_intro: Something brass and enormous ticks on Wrack Cave, and the sea moves when it does.
Its hands point at you. All of them.
dialogue_outro: The Tide-Clock winds down with a long sigh, and the sea around Wrack Cave settles to its own time.

encounters.name: The Moon-Blind Hermit
dialogue_intro: A hermit on Foam Foothills has stared at the moon until the moon stared back.
"It told me you'd come. It didn't say you'd lose."
dialogue_outro: The hermit blinks, and for a moment his eyes are his own. "Was it ever talking to me?"

encounters.name: Star-Pilgrim Oduya
dialogue_intro: A pilgrim has walked from the far side of the sky to Low Spire. She is not done walking.
"The heavens test everyone they meet. I am the heavens' errand."
dialogue_outro: Oduya bows. "You pass. The heavens will be insufferable about it."

encounters.name: Reeve Dunn of Harrowfield
dialogue_intro: Harrowfield: fields to every horizon, a road out that goes nowhere anyone has been, and nothing to do in the evenings but train.
The village reeve sets down his scythe and picks up a practice sword. "Fists up, lad. Hit me like the harvest's late."
dialogue_outro: Dunn spits and grins. "You'll bleed fine. Off to the Furrow with you."

encounters.name: Shieldbearer Orla
dialogue_intro: A traveller holds the ford on the Long Furrow, her tower shield planted in the mud.
"You want across? Go through me."
dialogue_outro: Orla hefts her dented shield onto her back. "Through me it is. Well fought, farmer."
lesson: GUARD
Attacks on an empty lane hit a GUARD creature first. Put one where you are open — and when the enemy has one, break it before you go for their Vigor.

encounters.name: The Old Smoke Golem
dialogue_intro: Old Smoke, the forge that burns with no fuel, has made itself a body out of its own slag and walked out.
It was built in the Old Age for a war nobody remembers. Nobody ever told it the war ended.
dialogue_outro: The furnace in its chest goes cold. The golem finally rests. Old Smoke burns on behind it.
lesson: ELITE
Elites start with more Vigor and pay out more: shards, a dig charge and stratum fragments. Build a board before you start trading.

encounters.name: The Cairn Hill Raiders
dialogue_intro: Raiders who heard a farm village was easy pickings come screaming down Cairn Hill.
"Grab what burns, leave the rest!"
dialogue_outro: The raiders wheel away over the hill, lighter by a few horses and a great deal of certainty.
lesson: SWIFT
SWIFT creatures can attack the turn they arrive. Keep a blocker up — and use your own to finish a foe that thinks it is safe.

encounters.name: Spearwife Halla
dialogue_intro: A Harrowfield mother with a boar-spear as long as two men waits at the Threshing Ring.
"Shields won't save you from this."
dialogue_outro: Halla plants her spear in the ring. "Huh. Maybe they would."
lesson: PIERCE
PIERCE: damage past a killed blocker carries on to the player. Chump-blocking with a tiny creature will not fully save you.

encounters.name: The Ashen Berserker
dialogue_intro: A man who trained in Harrowfield until there was nothing left of him but the training roars from the hilltop.
There is nothing left in him but the fight.
dialogue_outro: The berserker falls silent at last. Ash drifts down over the fields like snow.
lesson: ARMOR
ARMOR takes that much less damage from every hit. Many small hits do little — hit it once, and hit it hard.

encounters.name: Brannoc, Last Year's Champion
dialogue_intro: Last harvest's tourney champion stands on the bridge, alone by choice.
"I fight best with no one beside me."
dialogue_outro: Brannoc sits down on the bridge. "Maybe I'll try a friend next time."
lesson: EXALTED
Their first attacker each turn gets +1/+1 for each Exalted creature they control. Kill the Exalted ones and the big swing shrinks.

encounters.name: Warden Ironhand of the Threshing Ring
dialogue_intro: Every Harrowfield champion was made in the Threshing Ring, and one old man has judged every one of them.
"Every blade in this village was tested on my anvil. Now you."
dialogue_outro: Ironhand nods once. "Tempered. Now come up to Cairn Hill."
lesson: WARDEN
The keeper of this land. Wardens carry Relics too — each gathers charges and fires when full. Hold a card or Relic to read it.

encounters.name: Ironhand, the Cairn-Keeper
dialogue_intro: On Cairn Hill, where the first farmers were buried to sit on something, the ground is warm underfoot.
"Harrowfield was built on this hill for a reason. Nobody leaves it without knowing why."
dialogue_outro: The warmth under the hill fades to embers. "Harrowfield salutes you," Ironhand rasps. "The Cinderfall Steps are hotter still. Go and find out what nowhere is in the middle of."
lesson: BOSS RULES
Bosses bend the rules. Your leftmost lane starts buried and only opens when the boss's first creature dies — kill one early.

encounters.name: Plough-Giant Hobbe
dialogue_intro: On Forge Fang a farmer as tall as a barn is ploughing rocks.
"A furrow's got to run straight. You're in the way of straight."
dialogue_outro: Hobbe steps around you, and the furrow on Forge Fang bends for the first time in a hundred years.

encounters.name: The Scarecrow Muster
dialogue_intro: Scarecrows line Brass Delve in ranks, and one of them is giving orders.
"Crows we could stand. Crows and thieves we will not."
dialogue_outro: The scarecrows slump back onto their poles, satisfied that you are neither.

encounters.name: Cairn-Breaker Joss
dialogue_intro: Someone on Red Crag has been pulling down the old cairns for the stone.
"The dead don't need walls. I do."
dialogue_outro: Joss sets the last stone back on the cairn, grumbling. "Fine. Fine. I'll quarry."

encounters.name: Harvest-Queen Edda
dialogue_intro: The last sheaf on Copper Gate is crowned with poppies, and the woman wearing them carries a sickle.
"Every harvest takes a champion. This year it's going to take you."
dialogue_outro: Edda laughs and sets the poppy crown on your head. "Next year, then. Grow strong."
